The last Census showed that our city is home to more than 100 different ethnicities, Mayor Anita Baker says, so a further step in official accreditation is great news.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">What a day! ✨ Yesterday more than 300 business owners, entrepreneurs and business supporters came together for BizFest 2026 to learn, connect and build their village 🤝 

With the incredible <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/eteroa?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Namulau'ulu Nu’uali’i Eteroa Lafaele</a> bringing the energy all day long, BizFest was packed with inspiration, practical advice and powerful conversations.

Sir Ian Taylor’s journey is a remarkable reflection of New Zealand's technological and cultural evolution. Raised in a small East Coast village on the North Island, Ian experienced the arrival of electricity at his home at age seven in 1957, followed by the telephone a few years later.     <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Porirua’s status as a welcoming and inclusive place has received yet another boost ✅ 

The city received official accreditation from central government in 2024 as a Committed Welcoming Community, and the Council then co-created a Welcoming Plan with mana whenua Ngāti Toa, local groups and city officials, designed with Porirua's diverse communities in mind.

An assessment panel confirmed last week that the Council had successfully met the requirements to achieve Stage 2 "Established" Welcoming Community status. 

The last Census showed that our city is home to more than 100 different ethnicities, Mayor Anita Baker says, so a further step in official accreditation is great news.

"The first stage was about a commitment, a promise. But Stage 2 proves the Welcoming Plan isn’t just on paper, but actively working across our city, generating positive community outcomes in things like economic development, culture and identity, and accessibility to Council.

"Some of this is highlighted in initiatives and events, like the wonderful Lunar New Year celebrations we held at Aotea Lagoon in February, and Welcoming Week, last September, where people had the opportunity to connect, support and learn from each other."

Porirua City joined the Welcoming Communities programme in January 2023. It is one of 35 councils and five local boards in Aotearoa that participate in the programme.</p>
